name: Neural Network
description: Foundational artificial intelligence architecture inspired by biological neurons. Learns through gradient descent across layered weight matrices, discovering nonlinear mappings between input and output spaces. Embodies the principle that intelligence emerges from connection strength, not individual units.
training_paradigm: gradient-based optimization over differentiable loss surfaces

scope.definition: Training convergence efficiency of backpropagation on standard deep learning benchmarks — fraction of training runs achieving within 1% of best-known accuracy on CIFAR-10 within 100 epochs.

evidence.source: Rumelhart et al. (1986) 'Learning representations by back-propagating errors', Nature 323:533-536; LeCun et al. (2015) 'Deep learning', Nature 521:436-444.
cross_domain_examples: ResNet-20 with SGD+momentum: 91.7% CIFAR-10 accuracy in 200 epochs, reproducible across random seeds
backpropagation credit assignment enables training of networks 100+ layers deep — biological equivalent unknown
spiking neural networks with surrogate gradient: approximate backpropagation with 0.85 convergence rate

scope.falsifiability: If networks trained with alternative credit-assignment methods (local learning rules, feedback alignment) achieve statistically identical performance to backpropagation on standard benchmarks, backpropagation is not uniquely necessary.
scope.measurement_limits: Backpropagation requires exact gradient computation — not biologically plausible. Performance claims assume clean datasets; noisy labels or distribution shift degrade convergence. Random seeds introduce ±2% variance.

scope.definition: Feature hierarchy quality in deep networks — mutual information between intermediate layer representations and target labels, measured across layers of trained ResNet on ImageNet.

evidence.source: Zeiler & Fergus (2013) 'Visualizing and understanding convolutional networks', ECCV; Alain & Bengio (2016) 'Understanding intermediate layers', ICLR workshop.
cross_domain_examples: layer-by-layer mutual information with labels increases monotonically in trained deep networks
early layers: Gabor-filter-like features; middle layers: texture; deep layers: object parts — hierarchical structure
V1-V2-IT visual cortex hierarchy: analogous feature complexity progression from edges to objects

scope.falsifiability: If mutual information between intermediate representations and target labels decreases or is uniform across layers, the feature hierarchy is not forming progressively more task-relevant representations.
scope.measurement_limits: Mutual information estimation from high-dimensional representations is computationally challenging and sensitive to estimator choice. Interpretability of intermediate features degrades with network width and skip connections.

scope.definition: Training stability of SGD-based weight optimization — fraction of training runs where loss decreases monotonically (ignoring batch noise) over 80%+ of training epochs, across 5 architectures on CIFAR-10.

evidence.source: Sutskever et al. (2013) 'On the importance of initialization and momentum in deep learning', ICML; He et al. (2016) 'Deep residual learning', CVPR.
cross_domain_examples: SGD with momentum: loss trajectory shows consistent decrease in 0.87 of training runs with standard hyperparameters
Adam optimizer: faster initial convergence but 0.15 of runs show loss spikes or divergence on some architectures
gradient descent on convex functions: mathematical guarantee of convergence — neural network analogue is non-convex but empirically converges

scope.falsifiability: If loss curves for standard architectures on CIFAR-10 show random-walk behavior (no net decrease over 100 epochs) in >20% of training runs with standard hyperparameters, convergence is not reliable.
scope.measurement_limits: Convergence depends critically on learning rate, batch size, and weight initialization. Loss landscape has many flat regions (saddle points) that can slow but not prevent convergence with appropriate optimizers.
